title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
statement: Remove the n-th node counted from the end of a singly linked list (n = 1 is the last node) and return the head of the resulting list. n is always valid.

hints.1_question: Counting from the end is hard in one pass. What if one pointer is already n steps ahead of another?
hints.2_nudge: Give a fast pointer a head start of n nodes, then move both until fast reaches the last node. The slow pointer is then just before the node to remove.
hints.3_big_hint: Use a dummy node before head so removing the head is not special. fast and slow start at dummy; advance fast n times; while fast.next: move both; slow.next = slow.next.next; return dummy.next.

known_bugs.name: no dummy node (breaks when removing the first node)
known_bugs.followup: What are `fast` and `fast.next` if n equals the length of the list?

known_bugs.name: gap of n + 1 instead of n
known_bugs.followup: If fast leads by n+1 nodes and stops at the last node, which node is slow pointing at, and which node does slow.next skip?

known_bugs.name: returns the original head even if it was removed
known_bugs.followup: If the head itself was removed, is the old `head` variable still the head of the list?

followups: Why does a dummy node simplify the head case?
Can you do it with a single pass using only one pointer variable plus a counter? What changes?
